verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents self-hosting on your own infrastructure, including MongoDB, the API and the front-end, and a hands-on probe confirmed a working self-host roundtrip. That puts application data wherever you deploy it, and the warehouse-native design plus local-only targeting attributes keep event and user data in your own systems. However, no region or residency selection is documented for the managed GrowthBook Cloud, so choosing a location means running it yourself. Missing for 10: a documented region/data-residency choice for GrowthBook Cloud (e.g., EU vs US), and residency or compliance documentation for the managed offering.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
